test_title: PYST 19: SSC GD Constable 2024 - English (Held On: 24 Feb, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom

Between a rock and a hard place

options.text: Avoiding the main topic, not speaking directly about the issue
Stuck between two very bad options

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Between a rock and a hard place"** means being faced with two difficult choices, where either option can lead to a negative outcome. (कठिन परिस्थिति में फँसना) • **Example: **She was between a rock and a hard place when she had to choose between losing her job or moving to a different city. • **"Stuck between two very bad options"** refers to a situation where both available choices are undesirable. (दो बुरी स्थितियों के बीच फँसना) • **Example: **The company was stuck between two very bad options: either cut down on its workforce or shut down completely. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Avoiding the main topic, not speaking directly about the issue** (मुख्य विषय से बचना, सीधे मुद्दे पर बात न करना): • **Example:** Instead of addressing the problem, he kept avoiding the main topic. • **On the point of achievement** (उपलब्धि के कगार पर): • **Example:** She was on the point of achievement when she received the final approval for her project. • **Willing to do anything** (कुछ भी करने को तैयार): • **Example:** He was willing to do anything to get the job, even if it meant relocating to another country. 35:Tc48, The correct answer is: **Approval**.
